_comment: English script for the recorded (cold) demo, decisions of 2026-11-02 (docs/msr/ces2027_demo/cold_demo_2026-11-02.md). One persona: Junhyeok, who works at SK hynix MSR in Seoul, and his daughter Yuha. Seven past chats from November and December 2026; the demo is recorded on 2027-01-06 (DEMO_DATE in deploy/.env, a Wednesday), so 'this Saturday' is January 9 and 'Monday' is January 11. Every turn is short and states one fact with its relationship word ('my daughter Yuha'), because the search ranks single turns by embedding similarity and the LLM only sees the retrieved turns. demos: one topic per recording. The first question is asked verbatim in a chat with the no-memory model and again in a new chat with the memory model; the follow-up is chosen by whoever records, from follow_ups, by the condition in 'if', and must ask for facts the first answer did not contain, so that the second memory list differs from the first. expected: short word stems that must occur, as substrings, in the top-k memories (scripts/demo_check.py); stems rather than phrases, because the fact often comes back in a paraphrase ('swimming time' for 'swimming lesson') and demo_check.py matches substrings. no_memory: what the no-memory model is expected to do; asking back is a legitimate outcome. language and system_prompt are written into the Pipe valves by scripts/load_scenario.py. Dates carry the Las Vegas offset so the sidebar shows them as written; turns are one minute apart.
system_prompt: You are a helpful assistant. Keep every answer under 80 words, plain and concrete. Answer from what you know. Only when something essential is missing, say so in one sentence and ask one question.

sessions.title: Yuha's peanut allergy and school lunches

turns.content: My daughter Yuha has a peanut allergy, so every meal and every party menu at our house has to be peanut-free. Her school asked for safe lunch ideas. Can you help?

Of course. Peanut-free lunches for Yuha: kimbap without any peanut sauce, pasta salad with cherry tomatoes and mozzarella, egg rolls with rice, and cut fruit. Always check labels for 'may contain peanuts'.
She will eat anything with pasta, but she refuses mushrooms. Keep that in mind for any food you plan for her.
Noted: for Yuha, pasta is always welcome, mushrooms are out, and nothing with peanuts.
Yuha turns 7 on January 10 and she is obsessed with Frozen and Elsa. Her birthday party is at our apartment on Saturday, January 9, about twelve kids plus a few parents.
A Frozen party suits her: a snowflake hunt through the apartment, party food with winter names, and a paper crown for each guest. With twelve kids, two adults running the games keeps it calm.
She wants an ice castle cake like Elsa's palace for the party. How do I make one?

Stack two round vanilla cakes, cover them with pale blue frosting, stand ice cream cones on top as towers, and press rock candy and white chocolate shards around them so they shine like ice. A sparkler on the tallest tower gets the big reaction.
My daughter Yuha has a swimming lesson every Saturday from 10 to 11 at the pool in our neighbourhood, so Saturday plans for her have to start after lunch.
Noted: Saturday mornings are Yuha's swimming time, so anything planned for her on a Saturday starts in the afternoon.
She gets very hungry after swimming and tired by the early evening.
Then a late lunch right after the pool and nothing big after six in the evening works best for Yuha on Saturdays.
I am training for the Seoul Marathon in March. I run on Tuesday and Thursday mornings along the Han River before work and do my long run on Sunday. Can you build me a training plan?
A 16-week plan: Tuesday easy 5 km building to 8 km, Thursday intervals or tempo, Sunday long run from 8 km adding about 1 km a week up to 18 km, then a taper. Every fourth week is lighter.
My right knee gets sore after any run longer than 12 km. It is fine the next day.

Soreness that clears by the next day is a load issue, not an injury. Cap long runs at 12 km for two weeks, add 10 minutes of hip and quad strength work after Tuesday runs, and add no more than 1 km a week to the Sunday long run.
How do I keep the training going when I travel for a conference?
On a conference week keep Tuesday and Thursday as short easy runs wherever you are, and move the long run to a day you are home. Missing one long run does not hurt the plan.

sessions.title: Conference trip to Las Vegas in January

turns.content: Our team at SK hynix MSR is presenting at a conference in Las Vegas, so I fly there from January 11 to January 15. Sessions run all day, and I want to keep running during the trip.
Run early, before the sessions: most hotels there have a gym with treadmills, and the streets are quiet at six in the morning. Keep the runs short on a conference week.
Yuha asked me to bring her back an Elsa doll from the trip.
An Elsa doll is easy to find in the big toy stores there and packs flat in a suitcase, exactly what Yuha asked for.
Yuha's winter break starts on December 24. She wants to learn to skate like Elsa, and on cold days she needs indoor things to do.
Start with two or three short sessions at the Seoul Plaza skating rink, with a helmet and gloves. For cold days: a children's museum visit, baking together, and a library card.
She loved the skating. She also keeps asking to decorate her birthday cake herself.
Let Yuha decorate the ice castle cake: she can press the rock candy and sugar snowflakes onto the frosting once the towers stand.
I work from home on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays, and my lower back hurts after long days at the desk. I just bought a standing desk.
Alternate roughly forty minutes sitting and twenty standing, elbows at ninety degrees, monitor at eye level, and take a short walk every hour.
I want to use the home-office days for the strength work my running plan needs. I have a mat and a kettlebell at home.
On your home days do ten minutes of hip bridges, side planks and kettlebell deadlifts at lunch; it helps both the lower back and the knee stability your running plan asked for.
